purpose: Position the natural-prefix q-Apéry Plücker cap as a finite route-killing certificate in standard determinantal-divisor language, while preserving the separate moving-tail route.

classification.novelty_confidence: no_priority_claim; gcd monotonicity under adjoining two-by-two minors is routine determinantal-divisor arithmetic, while the displayed q-Apéry three-row anchor is a source-specific exact finite certificate
classification.recommended_terminology: natural-prefix determinantal-divisor cap (or early-minor gcd cap)
classification.significance: High as an architectural boundary and low as standalone novelty: it decisively retires the natural expanding-prefix compression route, so large adjacent minors cannot continue to absorb proof effort meant for a family-wide modulus.

primary_sources.title: Primitive sets in a lattice
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Lemma 3.2, printed p. 179, and Theorem 4.1, pp. 183-184, on gcds of maximal minors and their invariance under unimodular completion.
primary_sources.exact_source_locator: Printed p. 179 / extracted.md lines 323--328: Lemma 3.2 characterizes primitivity by gcd of maximal minors; printed pp. 183--184 / extracted.md lines 567--622: Theorem 4.1 and its correctness discussion give the unimodular Hermite-completion framework. The source supports standard determinantal-divisor context only.
primary_sources.supports: The standard determinantal-divisor and primitive-lattice framework in which a common divisor of minors is the relevant family-wide arithmetic invariant.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The q-Apéry row values, their gcd 6, the adjacent-depth contrast, or the moving-tail boundary.

primary_sources.title: On systems of linear indeterminate equations and congruences
primary_sources.author: Henry John Stephen Smith
primary_sources.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London 151 (1861)

primary_sources.does_not_support: A verbatim antecedent for the source-specific finite cap.

closest_known_result.statement: For a row family, the rank-two determinantal divisor is the gcd of its two-by-two minors; adjoining rows adds minors and hence can only decrease that gcd by divisibility.
closest_known_result.exact_delta: The local contribution is the exact primitive q-Apéry anchor w_0,w_1,w_2 with minor gcd 6 and the resulting decision that every natural prefix retaining it has 2- and 3-adic common depth at most one.

disconfirming_evidence.finding: Adjacent determinants can have growing 2- and 3-adic valuations even though the three-row family gcd is exactly 6.
disconfirming_evidence.effect: Reject the local-to-global inference from an adjacent exterior valuation to natural-prefix common compression.

disconfirming_evidence.finding: Discarding the early anchors changes the family and leaves a distinct moving-tail mechanism.
disconfirming_evidence.effect: The cap cannot be stated as a no-go for re-anchored tails or for analytic q-Apéry constructions.

claim_boundary.allowed_wording: An exact three-row q-Apéry certificate has rank-two determinantal divisor 6; every natural prefix retaining those rows has determinantal divisor dividing 6. This is a source-specific finite application of elementary determinantal-divisor monotonicity.
forbidden_wording: Growing adjacent determinants produce growing natural-prefix compression.
The finite anchor rules out moving-tail compression.
This formally proves a q-Apéry all-index theorem or irrationality at 3/2.
claim_boundary.open_boundary: A re-anchored moving-tail family still requires an all-index common-modulus theorem, controlled coefficient height, and analytic decay/nonvanishing evidence.

observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.comparison_relation: The family-wide rank-two determinantal divisor is the gcd of all two-by-two minors; adjoining rows can only decrease it. The q-Apéry row values and the gcd-6 anchor are a finite source-specific specialization, not a new Plücker-compression theorem.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.closest_known_result: Determinantal-divisor monotonicity and Smith-normal-form terminology are classical; the exact q-Apéry three-row certificate and its natural-prefix consequence were not located as an external named result.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.exact_delta: The finite anchor shows that every natural prefix retaining the first three rows has common divisor dividing 6, even when later adjacent determinants exhibit larger 2- or 3-adic valuations; this decisively separates local exterior growth from family-wide compression.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.disconfirming_evidence: The certificate is finite and only caps natural prefixes. Re-anchored moving tails, all-index valuation laws, height decay, and irrationality remain untouched; finite adjacent minors cannot pay the global height bill by themselves.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.confidence_ceiling: High for the exact finite cap and standard gcd monotonicity; low novelty/no priority claim; no moving-tail or #1049 endpoint implication.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.claim_ceiling: An exact three-row q-Apéry anchor has determinantal divisor 6, so every natural prefix containing it has divisor dividing 6. Do not generalize this to re-anchored tails, all-index valuations, or irrationality.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.hard_step: Construct and control a moving-tail family with an all-index common-modulus law, coefficient height, nonvanishing, and analytic decay simultaneously.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.open_boundary: Moving-tail compression and the full #1049 height/decay/irrationality route remain open.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.bounded_expert_act: Verify the three primitive row values and all pairwise minors in the pinned certificate, then check that any proposed prefix consumer literally retains those anchor rows.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.reentry_trigger: Re-enter if the packet, certificate, replay script, or reviewer card changes, or if a re-anchored moving-tail theorem appears.
